final_answer: Cervical spinal cord ALS samples show the strongest disease-duration correlations for CHIT1 (most negative, Spearman rho = -0.488, p = 1.57e-08), followed by SLC29A1 (rho = -0.467), MX2 (rho = -0.451), EPSTI1 (rho = -0.443), GNGT2 (rho = -0.439), TRIM38 (rho = -0.431), CD300LF (rho = -0.428), OAS1 (rho = -0.422), and IL17D (the strongest positive hit, rho = 0.419). In this cervical cohort, longer disease duration is therefore associated mainly with lower expression of microglial/innate-immune activation genes, with IL17D as the top positive outlier.
